aggressive_definition: Aggressive incident subtypes included advanced, high-grade, and fatal prostate cancer; the abstract also analyzed localized and low-grade disease separately.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: For antioxidant intake from supplements we found a positive association with total, advanced, localized, high grade and low grade prostate cancer in those above median supplemental TAC intake of users compared to non-users (Adjusted ORs for total prostate cancer: 1.37, 95 % CI 1.08-1.73, advanced: 1.51, 95 % CI 1.11-2.06, localized: 1.36. 95 % CI 1.06-1.76, high grade 1.60, 95 % CI 1.06-2.40, low grade 1.36, 95 % CI 1.03-1.81).
study_design: Population-based case-control study using food-frequency-questionnaire data from prostate cancer cases and controls.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: We used FFQ data from 1499 cases and 1112 controls in the population based case-control study Cancer of the Prostate in Sweden (CAPS).
reason: The abstract reports associations with total prostate cancer and with aggressive incident case subtypes, including advanced and high-grade disease. This was a retrospective population-based case-control study rather than a prospective cohort.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Antioxidant intake from all foods and from fruits and vegetables separately measured by the FRAP assay was not associated with prostate cancer risk.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied Q5-versus-Q1 estimate is for all/total prostate cancer. The abstract establishes the general endpoint for dietary antioxidant intake, although the exact numerical estimate is supplied by existing full-text evidence.
